overview.off:
In Original synthetic demo, Original plays with natural, healthy clarity: the warm synth bass pulse and rounded low chords sit comfortably alongside the central synth melody, while the chiming opening bells and crisp hi-hat ticks sparkle right up front without you needing to strain.

Tap Jump to clearest difference (0:06.8) and switch to Post-gig muffled or Permanent loss above — keeping your headphone volume fixed — to hear how loud music exposure dulls that crisp top edge while leaving the low beat strong.

overview.hiss:

answers.bass:
Right now Original is selected, so the warm synth bass pulse and rounded low chords and the chiming opening bells and crisp hi-hat ticks are both playing at their natural, balanced level.

When you switch to Post-gig muffled or Permanent loss and jump to 0:06.8, you will notice the warm synth bass pulse and rounded low chords stay almost just as loud because loud gigs wear down delicate high-note sensors in the inner ear long before deep bass sensors — which is why cranking your headphones only makes the bass boom.
answers.pub:
Even in an instrumental piece like Original synthetic demo, the chiming opening bells and crisp hi-hat ticks sit in the exact same clarity zone that carries sharp speech sounds like s, f, th, and t when following a friend’s conversation over bar music.

When those crisp edges fade while the warm synth bass pulse and rounded low chords stay loud, background pub chatter easily swamps conversations so voices sound loud enough yet blurry. Jump to 0:06.8 and toggle Original against Permanent loss to hear that crispness disappear and return.
answers.tinnitus:
During fuller, busier passages of Original synthetic demo around 0:06.8, the warm synth bass pulse and rounded low chords and the central synth melody give your brain plenty of outside sound to focus on, which naturally masks ringing or hiss.

When the arrangement opens up around 0:11.3, that outside cover drops away and internal ringing or hiss stands out starkly — the exact reason post-gig tinnitus feels loudest when you lie down in a quiet room. Select Ringing or Hiss under Tinnitus and jump between 0:06.8 and 0:11.3 to hear it.
answers.ears: Right now Original affects both left and right headphones equally in Original synthetic demo. You can click Right ear quieter above — or open Adjust ear levels to slide Left or Right down — then jump to 0:06.8 on headphones to feel how uneven hearing pulls instruments to one side.

You can easily hear the singer’s voice, yet words blend into each other instead of sounding sharp.

Turning your headphones up will not fix that lost crispness: raising the volume just makes the smooth electronic pulse and warm low pad boom uncomfortably in your ears while the blurred details stay fuzzy. Tap Jump to clearest difference (0:20.4) and switch between Original and Less treble at the same volume.

answers.pub:

Jump to 0:20.4 to listen closely to the vocals.
answers.tinnitus:
During fuller, busier passages of In Peace around 0:20.4, the smooth electronic pulse and warm low pad and Madam Snowflake’s gentle female lead vocal give your brain plenty of outside sound to focus on, which naturally masks ringing or hiss.
